# SuSiEOut

`SuSiEOut` implements SuSiE-OUT, a sparse summary-statistic fine-mapping
method for loci where a causal variant may have been omitted from the
tested set, for example by a minor allele frequency or SNP-only filter.
Each single effect can be null, assigned to a tested variant, or
assigned to an omitted variant (an OUT state). An omitted variant is
represented by its linkage disequilibrium (LD) fingerprint: its LD with
the tested variants, taken from a sequencing reference panel that
contains it.

In the code, arguments and fields named `examined_*` refer to tested
variants, and `excluded_*` or `outside_*` refer to omitted variants.

Full documentation, with a reference page for every function, is at
<https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/>.

## Acknowledgements

SuSiE-OUT builds on the Sum of Single Effects (SuSiE) model of Wang,
Sarkar, Carbonetto and Stephens (2020) and its summary-statistic
extension SuSiE-RSS (Zou, Carbonetto, Wang and Stephens, 2022), and uses
[`susieR`](https://github.com/stephenslab/susieR) as a reference
implementation. We are grateful to the SuSiE authors for making their
methods and software openly available. SuSiEOut is an independent
project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the SuSiE authors or
the `susieR` maintainers.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("weinstocklab/SuSiEOut")
```

## Example

``` r

library(SuSiEOut)
locus <- susieout_simulate_locus(1, architecture = "entirely_omitted")
fit <- susieout_fit(
    locus$z, locus$n, locus$R_analysis, locus$wgs_ld,
    locus$examined_ids, effect_prior = "robust_mixture", L = 10,
    count_prior = susieout_count_prior(lambda_total = 1,
                                       out_fraction = 0.10))
summary(fit)
susieout_credible_sets(fit)
```

### Locus plot

`plot(fit)` draws a LocusZoom-style view of the locus (see
[`susieout_locuszoom()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_locuszoom.md)):
tested variants at their position, coloured by r² with the lead variant;
the posterior inclusion probability of every tested (circle) and omitted
(triangle) variant, filled by credible set; and an optional gene track.
The subtitle reports the posterior probability that at least one causal
variant was omitted. It needs the suggested packages `ggplot2` and
`cowplot`.

``` r

ids <- c(fit$examined_ids, fit$excluded_ids)
positions <- setNames(1e6 + 2500 * seq_along(ids), ids)  # use real coordinates
plot(fit, positions = positions)
```

![Locus plot of a SuSiE-OUT fit](reference/figures/locuszoom.png)

Here the causal variant of a simulated locus was omitted. Evidence
spreads over its tested proxies and the omitted candidates (triangles)
instead of concentrating on one variant, and the plot shows a 45%
probability that a causal variant is missing. Positions of simulated
loci are arbitrary. Pass `genes =` a data frame with `gene_name`,
`start` and `end` columns for a gene track; the `gencode` table from
[gwasplot](https://github.com/weinstocklab/gwasplot), filtered to genes,
has these columns.

The dense nuisance parameter is total local infinitesimal variance, not
the coefficient placed directly on the z-score covariance. For `p`
tested variants and GWAS size `n`, `infinitesimal_variance = h2_dense`
fits

``` text
R + (n * h2_dense / p) R^2 + omega I.
```

This scaling lets the same local architecture be compared coherently
across GWAS sample sizes. Fixed fits report both `local_h2` and the
resulting `covariance_multiplier`; fixed variance fractions are not
labeled posterior probabilities.

The count prior is specified at the locus level. Changing `L` changes
the numerical approximation but not the prior probability that the locus
contains any sparse effect. `lambda_total` controls sparse-effect count
and `out_fraction` controls how that count is divided between tested
variants and omitted variants (OUT states).

Heterogeneous banks should not impose one sparse count or one positive
dense variance on every locus. Spike-and-grid averaging combines
sparse-count and nuisance states using a comparable variational
evidence. Here `training_loci` is a bank of loci with known causal
variants, such as those from
[`susieout_simulate_locus()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_simulate_locus.md);
see
[`?susieout_train_prior`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_train_prior.md)
for the required format:

``` r

sparse_prior <- susieout_train_prior(training_loci, em_iterations = 0)
nuisance_prior <- susieout_train_nuisance_grid(
    training_loci, sparse_prior,
    infinitesimal_grid = c(0, 0.002, 0.008, 0.032),
    ld_mismatch_grid = c(0, 0.04, 0.12))
prior_grid <- susieout_prior_grid()
fit <- susieout_fit_grid(
    locus$z, locus$n, locus$R_analysis, locus$wgs_ld,
    locus$examined_ids, trained_prior = sparse_prior,
    prior_grid = prior_grid, nuisance_prior = nuisance_prior)
```

`susieout_train_prior(..., em_update = "nuisance_only")` provides a
global EM diagnostic without feeding fitted OUT responsibilities back
into the count prior. A zero `out_fraction` fits a model that assumes no
causal variant was omitted and needs no LD fingerprints.

For large loci, `R_analysis` may be a `Matrix` sparse matrix. The sparse
backend avoids forming the full tested-by-tested LD matrix in dense form
and supports the `R + dI` nuisance covariance
(`infinitesimal_variance = 0`).

Josh Weinstock (<josh.weinstock@emory.edu>). See our other work at
[weinstocklab.org](https://weinstocklab.org).

# Package index

## Fitting

- [`susieout_fit()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit.md)
  : Fit the SuSiE-OUT fine-mapping model
- [`susieout_fit_grid()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit_grid.md)
  : Fit SuSiE-OUT by averaging sparse-count and nuisance states
- [`susieout_fit_nuisance_grid()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit_nuisance_grid.md)
  : Fit a SuSiE-OUT model averaged over local nuisance states
- [`susieout_fit_nuisance_grid_factorized()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit_nuisance_grid_factorized.md)
  : Fit the joint SuSiE-OUT nuisance model from a low-rank genotype
  reference

## Priors

- [`susieout_count_prior()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_count_prior.md)
  : Construct an L-invariant sparse-effect count prior
- [`susieout_effect_prior()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_effect_prior.md)
  : Construct an effect-size mixture prior
- [`susieout_prior_grid()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_prior_grid.md)
  : Construct a spike-and-grid sparse-effect prior

## Training priors

- [`susieout_train_prior()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_train_prior.md)
  : Train and freeze L-invariant SuSiE-OUT hyperparameters
- [`susieout_train_prior_grid()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_train_prior_grid.md)
  : Learn global sparse-grid weights from retained-data evidence
- [`susieout_train_nuisance_grid()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_train_nuisance_grid.md)
  : Learn a spike-and-grid nuisance prior from training loci
- [`susieout_calibrate_prior_grid()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_calibrate_prior_grid.md)
  : Calibrate sparse-grid weights with masked-WGS targets

## Summarizing and plotting fits

- [`summary(`*`<susieout_fit>`*`)`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit-methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.susieout_fit>`*`)`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit-methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<susieout_fit>`*`)`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit-methods.md)
  [`plot(`*`<susieout_fit>`*`)`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit-methods.md)
  [`predict(`*`<susieout_fit>`*`)`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_fit-methods.md)
  : Summarize, print, plot, and predict from a SuSiE-OUT fit
- [`susieout_locuszoom()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_locuszoom.md)
  : LocusZoom-style plot of a SuSiE-OUT fit
- [`susieout_candidate_support()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_candidate_support.md)
  : Variant support under SuSiE-OUT
- [`susieout_credible_sets()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_credible_sets.md)
  : SuSiE-OUT credible sets

## LD fingerprints

- [`susieout_candidate_mask()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_candidate_mask.md)
  : Apply realistic candidate-set masks
- [`susieout_harmonize_cross_ld()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_harmonize_cross_ld.md)
  : Harmonize WGS cross-LD rows to analysis alleles
- [`susieout_transform_fingerprints()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_transform_fingerprints.md)
  : Ridge-stabilized whitening and recoloring of WGS fingerprints
- [`susieout_bootstrap_fingerprints()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_bootstrap_fingerprints.md)
  : Bootstrap WGS cross-LD fingerprints

## Simulation and command line

- [`susieout_simulate_locus()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_simulate_locus.md)
  : Simulate a deterministic SuSiE-OUT locus
- [`susieout_cli()`](https://weinstocklab.github.io/SuSiEOut/reference/susieout_cli.md)
  : Command-line entry point for batch locus analysis
